title: Turning down a place in Basie's band out of fear
summary: When Herschel Evans died Basie telegraphed Cobb, who declined from fear at about seventeen or eighteen, staying with his loyal family band at Larkin's.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I play it for myself because I love it. That was a masterpiece (inaudible). I -- when Herschel died, I had the opportunity of going with that band. Basie sent me a telegraph. I was afraid. I had a lot of fear, and I was with my family band, Milton Larkin Hawkins, and I just told him I couldn't make it, I didn't think I was ready.
See, everybody thought I was ready, but I didn't have all the know-how. They thought I did, but I didn't have

it, and I had to just really get myself together to (inaudible) and I learned a lot in Hamp's band, the first man I work under, even when I left Milton in '42, but when they get me back in the '30s I was just afraid. I had a lot of fear, no assurance of myself. I just didn't feel like I could make it. I was just scared to venture out and go out there in them woods. That's what it was to me.
And you know what fear is, don't you? Fear is a son of a gun.
See, I was around 18 years old at this time, 17, 18, somewhere along there.

And I just wasn't ready for it. I was -- I wasn't even married then. I didn't get married until 20. And I -- I married in 39 and turned 21, married April, turned 21 in August that year. So this was prior to my marriage, and I was just afraid. But I knew who I was with (inaudible) because if they had a quarter, I had a quarter, we would divide that little money up, and that's the way we lived.
If one had a car, he was going to put some gas, everybody chip in and put gas in it. I picked the reed section up in my car, and they put gas in it to come to

rehearsal so we could rehearse together the reed section, but it made a good band, being with this loyalty to one another, and like a family and respected one another, and we had a good band. Sterling, not reedy, sterling. You're next.
